# GLOBAL PAY EQUITY & TRANSPARENCY STRATEGY FOR DISTRIBUTED WORKFORCE
## Balancing Location-Adjusted Bands, Internal Fairness, and Regulatory Compliance (2026+)

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Strategic Challenge:**

A 30-country remote workforce with location-adjusted pay bands faces three converging pressures:

1. **Internal Fairness Erosion**: Transparent salary comparisons (via Glassdoor, LinkedIn, Slack channels) undermine morale when similar roles pay 30–60% differently based on location
2. **Pay-Transparency Regulations** (EU, UK, Canada, US states): New laws mandate disclosure of pay bands, gender/ethnicity pay gaps, and salary justifications—exposing internal equity gaps
3. **Labor-Market Dynamics**: Real-time salary data (Levels.fyi, PayScale, Blind) makes location-adjusted logic increasingly indefensible to employees ("Why does Berlin engineer earning €55K when Toronto peer earns CAD $95K?")

**Core Tensions:**

| Tension | Stakeholder | Business Impact | Regulatory Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cost-of-Labor Optimization vs. Internal Equity** | Finance, Compensation, People | Location-adjusted bands reduce cost in lower-CoL markets (save 30–50% payroll in Poland, Portugal, India) but create perception of unfairness when roles are identical (e.g., "Senior Engineer" title, same work, different pay) | Pay-transparency laws increasingly view location-based differentials as discriminatory if not justified by substantive role differences |
| **Pay Transparency Mandates vs. Competitive Positioning** | Compensation, Legal, People | EU (2024+), UK (2024+), Canada (2024+), US states (CA 2022 expanded 2024; CO, NY emerging) require salary bands/ranges in job postings and pay-gap disclosures; competitor analysis data becomes public | Public disclosure of pay bands undermines negotiation leverage; competitors see your ranges; may trigger talent poaching ("We pay more") |
| **Role-Level Consistency vs. Location Flexibility** | Product, Eng, Finance | Remote work blurs location-based pay logic: engineer in Warsaw can perform identical work to Toronto peer; should they earn different pay? Yes (cost-of-living); but employees see identical responsibility + value delivered | Legal exposure: if location-pay difference not tied to substantive role differences, may constitute unlawful discrimination in some jurisdictions (emerging case law) |
| **Retention in High-CoL Markets vs. Retention in Low-CoL Markets** | People, Finance | Paying Toronto engineers 70% more than Warsaw engineers attracts talent to high-CoL markets but risks attrition in low-CoL markets ("Am I being paid less because I'm less valued?"); paradox: low-CoL markets may have deeper talent pool but pay less | Turnover risk in low-CoL markets; retention risk in high-CoL markets if non-competitive vs. local labor markets |
| **Algorithmic Consistency vs. Fairness Perceptions** | Compensation, Legal, Ethics | Current location-adjusted bands (e.g., "50% of SF rate" for Berlin) are transparent but arbitrary; employees perceive unfairness. Alternative: role-based + market-rate bands appear fairer but mask location-adjustment cost logic | Public scrutiny of pay-setting methodology; if algorithm appears arbitrary or biased (e.g., location proxies for demographics), regulatory risk (pay-discrimination claims) |
| **Global Consistency vs. Local Compliance** | Legal, Compensation | Unified global pay band would eliminate location-based friction but would be unaffordable (paying "Berlin" salary to all locations = massive payroll increase) or unsustainable (paying "Warsaw" salary globally = talent exodus from high-CoL markets) | Each jurisdiction has different pay-transparency requirements; global approach must accommodate multiple regulatory regimes |

---

## PART I: REGULATORY LANDSCAPE & PAY-TRANSPARENCY REQUIREMENTS

### 1.1 EU PAY-TRANSPARENCY DIRECTIVE (2024+)

**Legal Framework**: EU Pay Transparency Directive (Directive 2023/881), effective June 2024; implementation deadline June 2025 (member states)

**Scope**: All employers with ≥150 employees (EU-wide); applies to distributed EU workforce

#### **KEY COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS:**

| Requirement | Specification | Company Impact | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Salary Band Disclosure in Job Postings** | Employer must publish salary range (minimum and maximum) for all job postings; include non-monetary benefits | Job ads must show: "€40K–€65K" for "Senior Engineer" role (no hiding range); discloses internal pay structure | National labor authorities; employee right to sue for non-disclosure |
| **Request for Pay Explanation** | Employee may request written justification for pay decision (comparison to colleagues, market rate, role criteria); employer must respond within 1 month | Must prepare documented rationale for pay decisions (e.g., "Senior Engineer in Berlin paid €55K because: role scope includes team leadership [vs. peer IC], Berlin CoL €2,800/mo [cost index], market median €52K"); defensible documentation required | Employee litigation risk; labor authority investigation if patterns of pay discrimination detected |
| **Pay-Gap Reporting** | Employer with ≥150 employees must publish:  ① Gender pay gap (aggregated, not individual); ② Equal-pay audit (if gap >5%); ③ Action plan to close gap (if gap exists) | Exposes internal equity issues: if female employees paid 10% less on average, must disclose + justify + remediate; **problem: location-adjusted bands often correlate with demographics (e.g., more women in lower-CoL markets) = visible pay gap** | Public disclosure (government database + employer website); reputation risk; regulatory investigation if gap not addressed |
| **Intersectional Pay Gap** | Some EU countries (Germany, Italy) requiring gender × ethnicity pay gap reporting (emerging requirement) | Must track intersectional gaps: "Women in location X earning Y% less"; reveals if location-adjustment correlates with demographics | Regulatory scrutiny; public data (potentially searchable database) |
| **Pay Adjustment Transparency** | Employer must disclose factors influencing pay (role scope, experience, market rate, location, performance, etc.); if location is factor, must justify | If location-based pay differential used, must defend as job-related: e.g., "Location affects cost-of-living adjustment (+/- 20% based on CoL index)" acceptable; but "Pay varies by location arbitrarily" not defensible | Labor authority challenge; risk of pay-discrimination finding |
| **Promotion & Pay Progression Transparency** | Employer must disclose criteria for pay increases, promotions, bonuses; if location affects progression, must explain | If promotion pool in Berlin earns less than Toronto pool for same role, must justify (e.g., "Berlin market rate lower") | Legal challenge; regulatory investigation |

**Enforcement Mechanism**:
- **National Labor Authorities** (e.g., Germany BAG, France SNCL, Italy INPS): Investigate complaints; levy administrative fines
- **Penalties**: €2K–20K+ fines per violation (varies by country); escalates for systemic non-compliance
- **Employee private right of action**: Employees can sue employers directly for pay discrimination; can claim damages (back pay + compensation)
- **Data publication**: Pay-gap data likely to be publicly searchable (transparency intent)

**Timeline**:
- June 2024: Directive published; member states begin implementation
- June 2025: Deadline for national implementation; enforcement begins
- 2026+: First data collections; pay-gap reports published

**Impact Assessment for Remote Company**:
- **High exposure**: If Berlin, Warsaw, Lisbon offices pay differently for same role, must disclose + justify
- **Reputation risk**: Public pay-gap report showing location-based disparities will trigger internal/external scrutiny
- **Litigation risk**: Employees can request pay justification; if justification weak ("cost of living" without substantive role difference), litigation risk

---

### 1.2 UK PAY-TRANSPARENCY REQUIREMENTS (POST-BREXIT)

**Legal Framework**: Equality Act 2010 (gender pay-gap reporting); proposed expansions (2024) to include ethnicity + disability pay gaps; salary-band disclosure in job ads

**Key Requirements**:

| Requirement | Specification | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Gender Pay-Gap Reporting** | Employer with ≥250 UK employees must report gender pay gap (quarterly or annually, proposal varies) | Must disclose: "Female employees earn 8% less on average"; if gap >5%, action plan required |
| **Salary Band Disclosure** | Proposed law (Retained EU Law continuation): Job postings must show salary range | Similar to EU: "£40K–£65K" must be visible in job ads |
| **Ethnicity Pay-Gap Reporting** | Proposed (2024): Employers may be required to report ethnicity pay gaps (experimental; not law yet) | If enacted: must track pay disparities by ethnicity; remediation plan required |
| **Disability Pay Equity** | Emerging guidance: Consider disability pay gap reporting (voluntary, but increasing expectation) | Monitor pay for disabled employees; ensure no pay discrimination |

**Enforcement**:
- **Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC)**: Enforcement authority
- **Penalties**: Unlimited fines for pay discrimination; injunctions
- **Employment Tribunal**: Employees can sue directly; unlimited damages

**Timeline**:
- 2024–2025: Guidance issued; proposals debated
- 2025–2026: Implementation likely; first reporting deadlines

---

### 1.3 CANADA: PAY-TRANSPARENCY REQUIREMENTS (FEDERAL + PROVINCIAL)

**Legal Framework**: 
- **Federal** (Canada Labour Code): Employers with ≥100 employees must report gender pay gap (annual)
- **Ontario** (Pay Transparency Act, 2024): Employees have right to request pay information for comparable roles; employer must disclose
- **British Columbia, Alberta** (proposed): Similar pay-transparency laws emerging

**Key Requirements**:

| Requirement | Specification | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Gender Pay-Gap Reporting** | Federal employers: Annual reporting of gender pay gap; public disclosure | Exposes gap; remediation plan required if gap significant |
| **Pay Information Disclosure** | Ontario: Employee may request pay ranges for comparable positions; employer must provide within 30 days | Creates obligation to document pay ranges; defensible pay rationale required |
| **Salary Bands in Job Postings** | Proposed (multiple provinces): Include salary range in job postings | Similar to US California model: "CAD $80K–$130K" in ads |

**Enforcement**:
- **Labour authorities** (federal Canada Labour Relations Board; provincial ministries): Investigate complaints
- **Penalties**: Administrative fines CAD $5K–$50K+; compliance orders
- **Private litigation**: Employees may sue for pay discrimination

**Timeline**:
- Federal: 2024–2025 reporting underway
- Provincial: Ontario 2024 law effective; BC, Alberta 2025–2026

---

### 1.4 UNITED STATES: FRAGMENTED PAY-TRANSPARENCY LANDSCAPE

**Overall Pattern**: No comprehensive federal law; state + local patchwork

#### **TIER 1: STATE-LEVEL SALARY-RANGE DISCLOSURE LAWS**

| State | Law | Requirement | Effective | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **California** | SB-1228 (2022); expanded 2024 | Salary range (min, max, base + expected bonuses) in job postings; existing employees on request | 2023 (ongoing) | All employers; applies to CA jobs + remote roles in CA |
| **Colorado** | Equal Pay for Equal Work (2024 expansion) | Salary range in ads; employer must defend location-based pay differences | 2023–2024 | CO jobs + remote roles in CO |
| **New York** | Pay Transparency Law (2023) | Salary range in job postings; applies to remote roles affecting NY | 2024–2025 | NY jobs + remote roles in NY |
| **Washington** | Salary Range Law (2024 proposed) | Similar to CA/CO: salary range in postings | 2025+ (proposed) | WA jobs + remote |
| **Connecticut** | Pay Transparency Bill (2024 proposed) | Salary range disclosure | 2025+ (proposed) | CT jobs |

**Federal Level**:
- No comprehensive federal salary-range law (2024)
- **Executive Order (Biden, 2024 proposal)**: Would require federal contractors to disclose pay bands; not yet law
- **EEOC Pay Equity Guidance** (2023): Encourages employers to disclose pay ranges; not legally required

**Impact Assessment**:
- **High compliance burden**: If company has employees in CA, CO, NY, must disclose salary ranges in ads for any role that could be filled from those states
- **Practical consequence**: Remote company likely must publish salary ranges for most roles (since remote roles attract CA/CO/NY candidates)
- **Cascading effect**: Publishing ranges in US likely to trigger expectations in EU/Canada (fairness pressure even if not legally required)

### 1.5 OTHER JURISDICTIONS

| Jurisdiction | Pay-Transparency Status | Key Requirement | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Australia** | Fair Work Act (2024 amendments pending) | Voluntary pay transparency; growing pressure for salary-range disclosure | Low (guidance, not law yet) |
| **Brazil** | LGPD applies to pay data; labor laws under review | Data protection + emerging labor directives suggest pay-gap reporting coming | Medium (LGPD already enforced; labor rules evolving) |
| **India** | No pay-transparency law (2024); emerging labor code review | Growing pressure from NGOs; no legal requirement yet | Low (no enforcement mechanism yet) |
| **Singapore** | No pay-transparency law; employer discretion | Market-driven (tech companies voluntarily transparent to attract talent) | Low (voluntary) |
| **Poland** | EU Pay Transparency Directive applies | Same as EU: salary bands in ads + pay-gap reporting + pay justification | High (enforcement starts 2025) |
| **Portugal** | EU Pay Transparency Directive applies | Same as EU | High (enforcement starts 2025) |

## PART II: COMPENSATION STRATEGY REDESIGN

### 2.1 DIAGNOSIS: LIMITATIONS OF CURRENT LOCATION-ADJUSTED BANDS

**Current Approach (Typical Remote Company)**:

```
Base Role: "Senior Software Engineer"
Location Multipliers (% of San Francisco Base = $180K):

Toronto:      95% = $171,000
Berlin:       55% = $99,000
Warsaw:       40% = $72,000
Lisbon:       45% = $81,000
Singapore:    75% = $135,000
India:        25% = $45,000

Rationale: Multiply SF base by location cost-of-living index
```

**Problems with This Approach**:

| Problem | Manifestation | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Arbitrary Multipliers** | "Why 55% for Berlin? Why not 60%?" — No consistent methodology visible to employees | Perception of unfairness; legal defensibility weak (if challenged, must justify algorithm) |
| **Location as Proxy for Value** | Employees perceive: "I earn less because I live in Warsaw, not because my work is less valuable" | Morale erosion; retention risk in low-CoL markets; fair-pay litigation risk |
| **Correlation with Demographics** | Low-CoL markets (India, Eastern Europe) often have younger workforce or different gender distribution; location-based pay correlates with demographic pay gaps | Risk of inadvertent pay discrimination claim; transparency law exposure (pay-gap reports may show location × gender interaction) |
| **Unjustifiable under Transparency Laws** | EU Pay Transparency Directive requires defensible pay justification; "cost of living" alone may not suffice if role scope identical | Legal risk: employee requests pay explanation → company must justify; weak justification = litigation risk |
| **Talent Poaching Incentive** | Competitors see published salary ranges (US/EU transparency laws); poach talent from low-CoL markets ("We pay SF rates everywhere") | Retention risk in low-CoL markets; morale impact when employees learn competitor offers |
| **Inequitable Progression** | Bonus structure, stock options, benefits often tied to base salary; location-adjusted base creates cascading inequity (lower base = lower bonus, lower equity value) | Total compensation disparity (not just salary) widens location gap; perceived unfairness compounds |

---

### 2.2 RECOMMENDED APPROACH: "ROLE-BASED BANDS + LOCATION ADJUSTMENTS + MARKET BENCHMARKING"

#### **CORE PHILOSOPHY**

**Principle 1: Separate Role Value from Location Impact**
- Define pay bands by **role level + scope**, not location
- Apply location adjustments **transparently** as separate, justified component
- Rationale: "Your Senior Engineer role pays €50K–€70K globally; Warsaw location receives 80% of band (adjustment based on CoL); SF location receives 120% of band"

**Principle 2: Unified Global Bands, Location-Specific Variations**
- Same job title (e.g., "Senior Engineer") → same base band (global)
- Location determines where in band (and adjustment multiplier) employee is paid
- Rationale: Transparent, consistent, defensible under pay-transparency laws

**Principle 3: Market-Rate Anchoring**
- Bands anchored to **actual market salary data** (Levels.fyi, Payscale, industry surveys), not arbitrary multipliers
- Transparent benchmarking source (e.g., "Band set based on SF market median $180K, Berlin market median €60K")
- Rationale: Defensible under transparency laws; employees can verify band logic

**Principle 4: Defensible Pay Justification**
- Every employee's pay tied to documented factors:
  1. Role level (band)
  2. Location (adjustment)
  3. Experience/seniority (position in band)
  4. Performance (merit increases)
  5. Market movement (annual review)
- No arbitrary decisions; all defensible under "pay justification" requests

---

### 2.3 IMPLEMENTATION FRAMEWORK

#### **STEP 1: DEFINE ROLE-BASED BANDS (LOCATION-NEUTRAL)**

**Approach**:

Create unified global job architecture with **level-based bands** (not location-specific):

```
Job Family: Engineering
Career Progression:
├─ IC1 (Individual Contributor, Level 1): Junior Engineer
│  └─ Band: €40K–€55K (global reference band)
│     └─ Benchmarks: SF $95K–$130K | Berlin €40K–€55K | Warsaw €28K–€38K
│
├─ IC2 (Level 2): Mid-Level Engineer
│  └─ Band: €55K–€75K (global reference band)
│     └─ Benchmarks: SF $140K–$180K | Berlin €55K–€75K | Warsaw €38K–€50K
│
├─ IC3 (Level 3): Senior Engineer
│  └─ Band: €75K–€100K (global reference band)
│     └─ Benchmarks: SF $180K–$240K | Berlin €75K–€100K | Warsaw €50K–€65K
│
└─ IC4 (Level 4): Staff/Principal Engineer
   └─ Band: €100K–€140K (global reference band)
      └─ Benchmarks: SF $240K–$320K | Berlin €100K–€140K | Warsaw €65K–€85K
```

**Key Design Choices**:

1. **Reference Band Currency**: Choose **one global reference currency** (EUR recommended for distributed company):
   - All bands expressed in EUR (e.g., "€75K–€100K")
   - Location-specific benchmarks shown in local currency for transparency
   - Annual FX adjustments (if EUR strengthens/weakens, local-currency bands adjust, EUR band stays stable)

2. **Benchmarking Sources**:
   - **Salary.com, Levels.fyi, Payscale**: Public data for major locations
   - **Industry surveys** (Robert Half, Heidrick & Struggles): Specific tech roles
   - **Glassdoor, Indeed salary data**: Crowd-sourced market rates
   - **Methodology**: 50th percentile (median) for band midpoint; 25th–75th percentile for band range
   - **Transparency**: Publish methodology + sources to employees (defensible under transparency laws)

3. **Band Governance**:
   - **Update annually** (or after major FX movement)
   - **Review by**: Compensation + People Ops + Finance (cross-functional)
   - **Document**: Benchmarking data, sources, methodology → store in internal wiki/database

---

#### **STEP 2: DESIGN LOCATION ADJUSTMENT FRAMEWORK**

**Approach 1: Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA)**

```
Location Adjustment Formula:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Adjusted Salary = Base Band Midpoint × Location Multiplier

Where:
  Base Band Midpoint = global reference (EUR)
  Location Multiplier = CoL Index for location / CoL Index for reference city

Example:
  IC3 (Senior Engineer) Band Midpoint: €87,500
  
  Locations:
  ├─ Toronto: CoL Index 1.20 → €87,500 × 1.20 = €105,000 (~CAD $158K @1.5 FX)
  ├─ Berlin:  CoL Index 1.00 → €87,500 × 1.00 = €87,500
  ├─ Warsaw:  CoL Index 0.70 → €87,500 × 0.70 = €61,250
  └─ Singapore: CoL Index 1.15 → €87,500 × 1.15 = €100,625

CoL Index Source: Numbeo, Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU), or company-specific cost-of-living study
```

**Pros**:
- ✅ Defensible (tied to objective CoL data)
- ✅ Transparent (employees can verify CoL index)
- ✅ Equitable (same role earns proportional to living costs)

**Cons**:
- ❌ CoL data may not align with actual labor-market rates (e.g., Warsaw has lower CoL but competitive salary expectations if hiring from tech-savvy pool)
- ❌ Doesn't account for tax/benefit differences (Berlin has generous benefits, lower taxes → employees effectively earn more)

---

**Approach 2: Market-Rate Adjustment (Recommended)**

```
Location Adjustment Formula:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Adjusted Salary = Base Band Midpoint × (Location Market Rate / Reference Market Rate)

Example:
  IC3 (Senior Engineer) Band Based on SF Median: $210K

  ├─ Toronto Market Median: $155K → Multiplier = 155K / 210K = 0.74
  │   → Adjusted: €87,500 × 0.74 = €64,750 (local currency conversion + multiplier)
  │   [Conservative: only 74% of SF rate, not 95% as current approach]
  │
  ├─ Berlin Market Median: €85K → Multiplier = 85K / 100K = 0.85
  │   → Adjusted: €87,500 × 0.85 = €74,375
  │
  ├─ Warsaw Market Median: €52K → Multiplier = 52K / 100K = 0.52
  │   → Adjusted: €87,500 × 0.52 = €45,500
  │
  └─ Singapore Market Median: SGD 180K (€120K equiv) → Multiplier = 120K / 100K = 1.20
      → Adjusted: €87,500 × 1.20 = €105,000
```

**Pros**:
- ✅ Market-driven (reflects actual salary expectations in each location)
- ✅ Defensible (tied to public salary data)
- ✅ Competitive (aligns with what competitors pay, reducing poaching risk)
- ✅ Scalable (as markets evolve, adjustments reflect new reality)

**Cons**:
- ❌ May reveal that company pays below market in some locations (e.g., if Berlin market inflated by BigTech demand, company offer may be 20% below market)
- ❌ Creates multi-tier system: "Senior Engineer" in SF vs. Warsaw paid vastly differently, even if role identical

---

**Approach 3: Hybrid (Recommended Pragmatic Choice)**

```
Location Adjustment Framework:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Adjusted Salary = (Base Band Midpoint × Market-Rate Multiplier × 0.7) + (CoL Adjustment × 0.3)

Rationale:
  70% weight to market rates (what competitors pay; competitive positioning)
  30% weight to cost-of-living (genuine economic need adjustment)

Example:
  IC3 Band: €87,500
  
  ├─ Toronto:
  │   Market-Rate Multiplier: 0.85 (Toronto market slightly below global midpoint)
  │   CoL Multiplier: 1.15 (higher CoL in Toronto)
  │   Hybrid: (€87,500 × 0.85 × 0.7) + (€87,500 × 1.15 × 0.3)
  │         = (€52,063) + (€30,188) = €82,250
  │
  ├─ Berlin:
  │   Market-Rate Multiplier: 0.95
  │   CoL Multiplier: 1.00
  │   Hybrid: (€87,500 × 0.95 × 0.7) + (€87,500 × 1.00 × 0.3)
  │         = (€58,188) + (€26,250) = €84,438
  │
  └─ Warsaw:
      Market-Rate Multiplier: 0.60
      CoL Multiplier: 0.75
      Hybrid: (€87,500 × 0.60 × 0.7) + (€87,500 × 0.75 × 0.3)
            = (€36,750) + (€19,688) = €56,438
```

**Rationale for Hybrid**:
- Acknowledges both **market competition** (must pay competitively in high-demand markets like Toronto) and **genuine economic need** (Warsaw employees have lower living costs but deserve equity adjustment)
- Less dramatic pay gaps than pure market-rate (reduces perception of unfairness)
- Defensible under transparency laws (explicit dual-factor methodology)

---

#### **STEP 3: POSITION-IN-BAND FRAMEWORK (MERIT + SENIORITY)**

**Approach**: Once adjusted salary range determined per location, place each employee within band based on **experience + performance**, not location

```
IC3 Senior Engineer — Toronto
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Band Range: CAD $115K–$155K (adjusted from €82K–€110K based on Toronto rates)
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │  BAND: $115K ─────► $155K  ($40K range)  │
                 └─────────────────────────────────────────┘

Position in Band (each 25% increment):
├─ 25th %ile: $125K (Junior within level: 0–2 years in role)
├─ 50th %ile: $135K (Standard within level: 2–5 years in role)
├─ 75th %ile: $145K (Senior within level: 5–10 years in role)
└─ 90th %ile: $155K (Principal/expert within level: 10+ years)

Example Employee Placement:
  Name: Jane (Senior Engineer, Toronto, 4 years in role, "Exceeds Expectations" performance)
  → Position: 60th percentile (between 50th + 75th for 4-year tenure + performance)
  → Salary: $135K + (0.10 × $40K) = $139,000
```

**Key Principles**:
1. **Tenure + Performance**: Higher tenure + better performance → higher in band (not location)
2. **Transparent Placement Criteria**: Document why each employee in their band position
3. **Merit Increases**: Annual increases move employee within band (not between locations)
4. **Promotion Increases**: Promotion to IC4 (next level) → moved to 25th %ile of IC4 band

---

#### **STEP 4: ANNUAL MARKET ADJUSTMENT PROCESS**

**Approach**: Review + adjust bands annually to keep pace with labor-market movement

```
Annual Adjustment Cycle (Each Year):
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Q1: Market Data Collection
  └─ Gather 2024 salary data from Levels.fyi, Payscale, industry surveys
    └─ Calculate new market medians per role + location

Q2: Band Recalibration
  └─ Update band midpoints based on new market data
  └─ If market moved +5%, adjust band +5%
  └─ Ensure all employees remain within updated band (if not, discuss adjustment)

Q3: Individual Merit Reviews
  └─ Review each employee: position in band appropriate?
  └─ Performance-based adjustments (merit raises within band)
  └─ Promotions (move to next band level)

Q4: Communication + Implementation
  └─ Announce new band ranges + any individual adjustments
  └─ Transparency: "Markets rose 4% globally; your role band adjusted 4%"
```

### 2.4 PAY-TRANSPARENCY COMPLIANCE INTEGRATION

#### **EU PAY TRANSPARENCY DIRECTIVE COMPLIANCE**

**Requirement 1: Salary Bands in Job Postings**

```
Current Job Ad:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Position: Senior Software Engineer (Remote, EU)
Salary: Competitive
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Compliant Job Ad:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Position: Senior Software Engineer (Remote, EU)
Level: IC3 (Senior Engineer)

Salary Range (by location):
├─ Germany: €75,000–€100,000
├─ France: €77,000–€102,000
├─ Poland: €52,000–€68,000
├─ Spain: €60,000–€80,000
└─ Italy: €58,000–€77,000

Salary Methodology:
  Base band (€75K–€100K) adjusted per location based on:
  • Market salary data (Levels.fyi, Payscale)
  • Cost of living index
  • Benefits/tax environment

Benefits (included in total compensation):
  ├─ Healthcare (country-specific)
  ├─ Pension/401k (country-specific matching)
  ├─ Remote work stipend: €1,200/year
  └─ Professional development: €1,500/year
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

**Requirement 2: Pay Justification Document**

**Internal Document** (shared with employee on request per Directive Article 6):

```
PAY JUSTIFICATION MEMO
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Employee: Jana (Senior Engineer, Warsaw)
Current Salary: €62,000/year
Date Requested: Jan 2026
Response Date: Feb 2026 (within 30 days)

Job Level & Band:
  Role: Senior Software Engineer (IC3)
  Global Band: €75,000–€100,000 (50th percentile: €87,500)
  Rationale: Based on SF market median ($210K) + global senior eng roles

Location Adjustment:
  Warsaw Location Multiplier: 0.65 (market rate 65% of global median)
  Adjusted Band: €48,750–€65,000 (midpoint: €56,875)
  Market Data Source: Levels.fyi 2025 Polish market survey (n=150 responses)
                      Payscale Poland senior engineer median: €52,000

Position in Band:
  Jana's Tenure: 3 years in role (Senior IC3)
  Performance Rating: "Exceeds Expectations" (top 20%)
  Placement: 70th percentile within Warsaw band
  Calculation: €48,750 + (0.70 × €16,250) = €60,875 → rounded €62,000
  
Comparability Analysis:
  Comparable Peers (similar level, tenure, performance):
  ├─ Peer A (Berlin, 3yr tenure, Exceeds): €72,000 ✓ (higher CoL, higher band)
  ├─ Peer B (Warsaw, 4yr tenure, Exceeds): €65,500 (slightly higher tenure)
